hook.line: Altamira's people are friendly, a little too friendly. When Don Hernando wants to warn Tomás without sounding dramatic, he reaches for the little word every Colombian uses to say "careful".

examples.es: Te advierto que no me voy a quedar callado.
examples.en: I'm warning you, I'm not going to keep quiet. (to a friend)

examples.es: Si no pagas el arriendo, te saco.
examples.en: If you don't pay the rent, I'll throw you out. (to a friend)

examples.es: Si no lo terminas mañana, estás despedido.
examples.en: If you don't finish it tomorrow, you're fired. (to one person)

rule:
Four ways to warn, from friendly to harsh:

*¡Ojo con…!* Short and everyday: "watch out for" a thing, right now.
*No confíes en…* or *No te fíes de…*: "don't trust" someone, from now on. Note the little words *en* and *de*.
*Te advierto que…* followed by a plain fact: "I'm warning you that".
*Si no…, …* a threat. The verbs stay plain, with no "imagined" form, because you are sure of what will happen.

To a group, *No confíen en él*. To someone you call *usted*, *No confíe en él*.
smallPrint: Teachers call *no confíes* a negative command: *no* plus the *tú* form that ends in *-es*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *confíes* or *confías*. To a friend: No ___ en él. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: After *no*, an order to *tú* ends in *-es*: *confíes*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *confíe* or *confíen*. To a group of friends: No ___ en él. Type the whole sentence.

yourTurn.why: *Ojo con* plus the thing you want them to watch.

yourTurn.prompt: I'm warning you, I'm not going to keep quiet. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Te advierto que no me voy a quedar callado.
accept: Te advierto que no voy a quedarme callado.
yourTurn.why: *Te advierto que* plus a plain, sure fact.

yourTurn.prompt: If you don't pay the rent, I'll throw you out. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Si no pagas el arriendo, te saco.
yourTurn.why: *Si no* plus plain verbs: you are sure of the consequence.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it formal: No confíes en él. Say it to someone you call *usted*.
Make it about you all: Si no lo terminas mañana, estás despedido. Say: If you all don't finish it tomorrow, you're fired.
yourTurn.answer: Si no lo terminan mañana, están despedidos.

pitfalls.why: Almost. The warning word is always followed by *con*.
As an order to a friend, the verb takes *-es*; *confías* would only state a fact.

personal: Think of a real warning you'd give a friend, then say it: *Ojo con…* or *No confíes en…*
